findings.issue_text: [BUG] assignment_source.to_dict() embeds a raw datetime ('queued': timezone.now()) into celery task kwargs passed to sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async, which cannot round-trip through the broker's JSON task serializer. On every inbound-driven assignment (e.g. a Jira webhook calling sync_group_assignee_inbound -> GroupAssignee.objects.assign(assignment_source=...) -> sync_group_assignee_outbound), apply_async raises a kombu EncodeError/TypeError while serializing the datetime in the producer (web/consumer) process, so the outbound assignee sync task is never enqueued and the inbound assignment webhook errors. The new tests pass only because self.tasks() executes the task inline without broker serialization, masking the failure.

[BUG] The dataclass default 'queued: datetime = timezone.now()' is evaluated once at module import time, so every AssignmentSource instance created for the life of the process carries the same import-time timestamp. The 'queued' field records when the worker/web process imported the module, not when the assignment was sourced; any consumer relying on it to order or age assignment events gets a stale, meaningless value. test_to_dict only asserts 'queued is not None', so the defect is invisible to the test suite.

[ADVISORY] The sync_assignee_outbound celery task gains a new kwarg 'assignment_source_dict', producing a rolling-deploy skew where web nodes on new code enqueue kwargs that workers on old code reject. During a rolling deploy, any worker still running the old task signature (def sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue_id, user_id, assign)) raises TypeError on tasks enqueued with assignment_source_dict, so outbound assignee syncs triggered by inbound webhooks fail (and after retries, are dropped) until all workers are updated.

[ADVISORY] The 'queued' field is ships-inert: it is populated, serialized into every task kwargs payload, and deserialized by from_dict, but no code in this diff (or any caller of should_sync/sync_assignee_outbound) ever reads it. Every outbound assignment pays the serialization/transport cost of a datetime that nothing consumes, and (per the import-time default defect) the value it carries is wrong anyway; future maintainers may trust it as an ordering signal when it is not one.

[BUG] The dataclass default `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated exactly once at module import time, so every AssignmentSource constructed without an explicit `queued` (i.e., every one created via `from_integration`, the only constructor used in this diff) carries the same import-time timestamp instead of its actual creation time. The `queued` field — which exists precisely to timestamp when a sync originated, the primitive needed to bound sync loops — is meaningless: all sources created in a process share the module-load instant, and the value differs per worker depending on when each process imported the module. Any consumer (including the tests' `queued is not None` assertion, which cannot detect this) reads garbage. This is a mechanical Python dataclass pitfall: defaults are evaluated at class-definition time, not per-instantiation.

[BUG] The cycle guard only suppresses the direct source integration, so a two-integration ping-pong (issue linked to both Jira and GitHub with outbound assignee sync enabled on both) loops indefinitely: Jira's inbound assign fans out to GitHub, GitHub's inbound assign fans back to Jira (source integration_id ≠ Jira's, so should_sync passes), forever. The comment claims 'prevent sync-cycles from occurring' but the implementation only prevents self-echo. Each leg of the A↔B loop generates webhooks that re-trigger the other leg with a different source, producing unbounded assign/unassign churn on both external systems. The `queued` timestamp field — the natural mechanism to bound such multi-hop loops — is written by this diff but read by nothing, confirming the loop-bound half of the design was never implemented.

[ADVISORY] The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature gains an `assignment_source` parameter, but no caller in this diff ever passes it — the resolve/unresolve and inbound-status paths still invoke should_sync source-less — so the cycle prevention this PR claims applies only to assignees, not to status synchronization. Status sync has the identical bounce topology (Jira resolve → Sentry resolve → GitHub resolve → Jira...) and remains unguarded. A future reader wiring status sync will assume the parameter threading exists because the signature advertises it, and the dead parameter rots until someone either wires it or removes it. The PR title 'cross-system issue synchronization' over-delivers relative to what the diff actually protects.

[ADVISORY] The `apply_async` kwargs dict now always includes the `assignment_source_dict` key (even when the value is None), so every outbound-assignee task enqueued by new code carries a kwarg that the previous task signature `sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue_id, user_id, assign)` does not accept. During a rolling deploy, old workers execute these messages and raise TypeError on the unexpected kwarg, failing the task — outbound assignee sync silently stops for the whole deploy window, and this applies to all user-driven assignments (the key is sent even when no source exists), not just integration-sourced ones. The new parameter needed a **kwargs-style backward-compatible signature or a deploy-ordering note; neither is present.

[ADVISORY] `to_dict()` emits `queued` as a datetime, but the Celery/kombu JSON transport serializes it to an ISO string and `from_dict` (`cls(**input_dict)`) silently accepts the string, so the reconstructed AssignmentSource has `queued` typed as `str`, violating the dataclass declaration. Any consumer that relies on `queued` being a datetime (comparison, arithmetic for staleness) crashes with a TypeError on worker-reconstructed instances while working on producer-side instances — a producer/consumer asymmetry that no test in the diff exercises because the round-trip through serialization is bypassed by the model tests that mock the integration method and run tasks eagerly.

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` returns None on any malformed payload (caught ValueError/TypeError), silently downgrading a corrupted or schema-skewed source to 'no source', which disables the cycle guard for that sync rather than failing it. During version skew or if the producer's dict shape ever changes (e.g., an added required field or renamed key), the worker logs nothing, the guard is bypassed, and the self-echo assignment the feature exists to prevent bounces back to the external system. A malformed cycle-guard credential should be loud, not treated as 'user-initiated'.

[ADVISORY] The new cycle test covers only the matching-source case (assert_not_called) and the source-less case; the code comment's explicit claim that 'other integrations [should] propagate changes outward' — a non-matching source still syncing — has no assertion anywhere in the diff's tests. A regression that inverts the guard (blocking all sourced outbound syncs, or comparing against the wrong id such that foreign sources are also blocked) passes the entire suite, since no test exercises a sourced assignment whose integration_id differs from the target integration. The negative case protecting the feature's core value proposition is the one case left unverified.

[BUG] The cycle check in should_sync only suppresses outbound sync when the source integration is the same integration, so the claimed invariant 'prevent sync-cycles from occurring' is not enforced for cycles of length >= 2. A group linked to two integrations that both have assignee inbound+outbound sync enabled ping-pongs forever: assign in integration X -> inbound webhook (source=X) -> outbound to Y allowed (Y != X) -> Y's external system updated -> Y's inbound webhook (source=Y) -> outbound to X allowed (X != Y) -> X updated -> repeat. GroupAssignee.assign re-fires sync_group_assignee_outbound even on re-assignment of the same user (the sync call precedes the `if not created` branch), so every echo is a fresh outbound task. The check at line 387 compares sync_source.integration_id only against self, never against the set of integrations already visited for this assignment, so the stated cycle-prevention guarantee is only a self-echo guard.

[ADVISORY] sync_group_assignee_outbound now always includes the assignment_source_dict key in the Celery kwargs (even when its value is None), which breaks old workers during a rolling deploy. Old worker processes still running the previous task signature `sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue_id, user_id, assign)` raise TypeError on the unexpected keyword argument for every assignment task enqueued by a new web node during the deploy window, failing (and retrying/final-failing) all outbound assignee syncs until workers are rolled. Making the key conditional on assignment_source being non-None (or tolerating the kwarg in the old signature) avoids the skew.

[ADVISORY] sync_status_outbound gains an assignment_source parameter that no call site in this diff ever passes, while the sibling abstract sync_assignee_outbound — which the task DOES call with assignment_source — was not given the parameter in its abstract signature. Untraceable plumbing in both directions: the status parameter is dead code a future reader will assume is wired up, and the assignee abstract interface relies on concrete implementations' **kwargs to accept a kwarg its own contract does not declare — any integration override that spells out its parameters without **kwargs crashes with TypeError when the outbound task passes assignment_source. The two abstract signatures should be consistent and each parameter should have a real producer or not exist.

[ADVISORY] The inbound unassign path (deassign with a constructed AssignmentSource) added in this diff has no test coverage in this diff — the new tests only cover the outbound-task suppression for the assign direction and the assignment_source=None propagation for direct assign/deassign. A regression that drops the assignment_source kwarg from this deassign call (or from GroupAssignee.deassign's propagation) silently disables cycle suppression for every integration-driven unassign, and no test in the diff would catch it — the failure mode is the exact sync-echo loop this PR exists to prevent, resurfacing only on the unassign path in production.

[BUG] sync_group_assignee_outbound serializes a raw datetime into Celery task kwargs: AssignmentSource.to_dict() uses dataclasses.asdict, which emits the `queued` field as a datetime object, and apply_async's JSON serializer cannot encode datetime, so the task publish raises instead of enqueueing. Every inbound-driven outbound sync that carries a source (sync_group_assignee_inbound -> GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign(assignment_source=...) -> this apply_async) fails at publish time; the EncodeError propagates synchronously back through deassign/assign into the inbound webhook handler, so external->Sentry assignment sync now crashes the whole inbound sync path instead of propagating the assignment.

[BUG] `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at module import, not per instantiation, so every AssignmentSource created via from_integration carries the process-start timestamp rather than the assignment time. The field's meaning is silently wrong for the entire lifetime of each worker/web process (all sources share one timestamp); any consumer that later trusts `queued` for ordering, dedup, or cycle-window logic gets garbage, and the unit test (assert queued is not None) cannot detect it because the import-time value is non-None. It also guarantees the datetime is present in every to_dict() payload, feeding the serialization failure in sync.py.

[ADVISORY] New required kwarg assignment_source_dict is added to the sync_assignee_outbound task signature with no **kwargs fallback, so producers and workers cannot coexist during a rolling deploy. During the deploy window, web nodes running the new code enqueue kwargs that old workers' sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue_id, user_id, assign) rejects with TypeError; outbound assignee sync is dropped for every assignment performed until all workers are updated — a silent failure window the rollout cannot avoid.

[ADVISORY] The assignment_source parameter added to the sync_status_outbound abstract method has no producer anywhere in this diff — no caller (e.g. the sync_status_inbound task) passes it, and should_sync's cycle guard is only reachable for the outbound_assignee attribute. Status-sync cycles (Sentry resolve -> external resolve -> inbound webhook -> Sentry) remain unguarded while assignee cycles are guarded; the dead parameter signals the cycle problem is 'handled' at the interface level, so the next implementer wiring status sync will assume the guard applies when it never fires, and a real A->B->A status loop can still ping-pong indefinitely.

[ADVISORY] from_dict collapses 'payload unparseable' and 'no source' into the same None sentinel, and any unknown key in the payload (ValueError/TypeError from cls(**input_dict)) disables the cycle guard for that message. When a future producer adds a field to AssignmentSource (or the payload is corrupted in transport), old consumers' from_dict returns None, should_sync sees no source, and the outbound sync proceeds — re-enabling the exact sync-cycle this PR exists to prevent, silently and per-message; there is no log or metric distinguishing the two Nones.

[ADVISORY] The only test that passes a non-None assignment_source exercises the blocked path (assert_not_called); no test enqueues the outbound task with a source present, so the source-bearing happy path is untested and CI stays green while the datetime-kwargs serialization failure fires in production. A regression in the enqueue-with-source path (which is exactly where the datetime bug lives) is invisible to the suite: the matching-source test green-lights the PR while every real inbound assignment with a resolvable user fails at task publish.

[BUG] assignment_source.to_dict() embeds the raw `queued: datetime` field into celery task kwargs, and the JSON task transport cannot serialize a datetime, so apply_async raises at publish time. Every inbound-triggered outbound assignee sync (sync_group_assignee_inbound now always constructs a source via from_integration on both the assign and deassign branches) crashes when enqueueing sync_assignee_outbound, so inbound assignment sync from integrations fails entirely; tests pass only because self.tasks() executes inline without broker serialization, hiding the failure. The datetime must be serialized to a string in to_dict (or dropped) before crossing the queue boundary.

[BUG] The dataclass field default `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at module import time, so every AssignmentSource constructed without an explicit queued value carries the server process's startup timestamp, not its actual queue time. The field's purpose (recording when the assignment was queued) is silently wrong for every instance; any future consumer trusting `queued` gets a timestamp that can be days stale. It also feeds the broken datetime payload in sync.py. The default must be a sentinel plus __post_init__/default_factory, or the field dropped — nothing in this diff reads it anyway.

[ADVISORY] The abstract sync_status_outbound signature gained an `assignment_source` parameter that no call site in this diff passes, and no status-sync path (sync_status_inbound, resolve/unresolve) threads a source at all — the PR's stated goal of preventing sync cycles is implemented only for the assignee path. The objective silently narrowed from 'cross-system issue synchronization' with cycle prevention to assignment-only cycle suppression without a recorded acceptance of that narrowing; status changes still echo between linked systems (the exact loop class the comment at mixins/issues.py:386-388 claims to prevent), and the inert parameter invites out-of-tree implementers to accept a value that nothing sends.

[ADVISORY] The sync_assignee_outbound task gains a new kwarg (assignment_source_dict) that new producers send immediately, but workers running the pre-deploy task signature raise TypeError on the unrecognized kwarg. During any rolling deploy window, every outbound assignee sync enqueued by new web/task nodes fails on old workers instead of syncing — the previously-working sync path degrades during rollout, and the failures surface as generic task errors rather than a deploy-skew signal.

[ADVISORY] AssignmentSource.from_dict swallows ValueError/TypeError and returns None with no logging, so any payload-shape drift or version skew silently degrades to 'no source' and should_sync proceeds as if cycle suppression never existed. The loop-prevention mechanism fails open and invisibly: the moment the dataclass shape evolves (or a producer/worker skew produces a mismatched dict), sync cycles resume with zero diagnostic signal — the exact regression this PR exists to prevent returns silently and is indistinguishable from the feature working correctly.

[ADVISORY] The only new behavioral test exercises the suppression path in-process (assert_not_called); no test covers a source from a different integration surviving the to_dict -> task -> from_dict round trip and correctly allowing the outbound sync, nor a deassign-with-source suppression case. The pass-through path — the path every non-echo assignment actually takes in production — is untested, and per the serialization defect it is currently broken; a future regression in the round trip would silently disable or invert cycle suppression with no failing test.

[BUG] The dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates `timezone.now()` once at module import, so every AssignmentSource created via `from_integration` carries the process's import-time timestamp instead of the actual assignment time. All AssignmentSource instances in a long-running worker share one stale `queued` value; any consumer ordering or auditing assignments by `queued` gets meaningless data (every assignment appears to have occurred at worker startup), and the timestamp silently drifts as workers restart.

[BUG] The `assignment_source.to_dict()` payload includes the `queued` datetime object and is passed directly as Celery task kwargs to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async`, which fails JSON serialization and breaks the outbound sync task enqueue. Every assignment that flows through the new source-tracking path (inbound sync -> GroupAssignee.assign -> sync_group_assignee_outbound -> apply_async) raises EncodeError in kombu's JSON serializer at enqueue time, so the outbound assignment task never runs and the sync feature is broken for all sourced assignments, with the exception propagating into the calling inbound-sync task.

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` silently returns None for any dict whose shape drifts (renamed/missing/extra field), which degrades the task into the pre-fix behavior where the cycle-suppression check in `should_sync` is skipped entirely. If the serialized AssignmentSource shape ever changes (e.g., a field rename or a serializer that converts `queued` to a string rejected by the constructor), the malformed payload is swallowed without any log line, the sync-cycle guard silently turns off, and operators see re-emergent integration assignment ping-pong with no diagnostic pointing at the deserialization failure.

[ADVISORY] The cycle-prevention check only suppresses sync when the source integration equals the target integration, so a pair of integrations that mirror each other's assignments (A assigns -> B receives -> B webhook -> A receives -> A webhook -> ...) still loops infinitely despite source tracking now being available to detect it. Customers with two mutually-syncing integrations (e.g., Jira and GitHub both configured for assignee sync on the same issues) get an unbounded assign/unassign ping-pong across both external systems, generating duplicate API calls and webhook storms; the new AssignmentSource data was specifically introduced for cycle detection but is only used for the trivial self-cycle case.

[ADVISORY] The task signature gains a new `assignment_source_dict` kwarg that pre-deploy worker code does not accept, so during a rolling deploy new producers enqueue tasks old workers cannot execute. During the deploy window, inbound-sourced assignments produce `sync_assignee_outbound` messages containing the new kwarg; old workers raise TypeError when invoking the task with an unexpected keyword argument, dropping outbound assignment syncs for the duration of the rollout instead of degrading gracefully.

[ADVISORY] The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature gains an `assignment_source` parameter that no caller in this diff ever supplies, adding dead API surface that every concrete integration subclass must now carry. Implementers of IssueSyncIntegration are forced to accept and thread a parameter that is always None in this change; if status-sync cycle prevention is later needed, each subclass will have independently ignored or half-threaded the parameter, making the eventual fix harder and the current signature misleading about supported behavior.

[BUG] The dataclass field default `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class-definition (module import) time, so every AssignmentSource instance ever created carries the same deploy/import timestamp instead of the time the assignment was actually queued. All `queued` values recorded via to_dict()/from_dict() round-trips are the worker's import-time timestamp, not the real enqueue time; the field is meaningless as audit metadata. Mechanically verifiable dataclass semantics: class-body defaults execute once.

[ADVISORY] test_to_dict asserts only `result.get("queued") is not None` — an existence check with no value, type, or freshness assertion — so it passes even though the `queued` default is frozen at module import time (the bug it should have caught). The test suite grants false confidence on the one field whose value is actually wrong; a staff reviewer would assert `queued` is a datetime near `timezone.now()` at construction time, which would fail today and expose the stale-default defect.

[BUG] The new code ships `assignment_source.to_dict()` — which contains a raw `datetime` (`queued`) — directly into Celery `apply_async` kwargs, and no test in the diff exercises the to_dict → queue → from_dict round-trip, so the serialization behavior of the actual transport is completely unverified. If the Celery task serializer cannot encode datetime (kombu's default JSON encoder raises EncodeError), every inbound-webhook-triggered assign/deassign that now passes an assignment_source fails at publish time and the outbound sync silently never happens; if a custom encoder stringifies it, from_dict accepts a string `queued` with no validation. The new tests cannot catch either outcome: test_assignment_source.py only feeds from_dict hand-built dicts (`{"source_name": ..., "integration_id": ...}`) that omit the `queued` key, and test_groupassignee.py exercises the matching-source path without asserting anything about the kwargs actually published to the queue.

[ADVISORY] The new cycle-prevention branch in should_sync is only tested for its blocking case (same-integration source → not called); no test passes an AssignmentSource from a *different* integration, nor exercises the deassign path with a source, so the 'other integrations propagate changes outward' behavior the code comment promises is unverified. A regression that over-blocks — e.g. the condition degrading to `if sync_source: return False` — would suppress all outbound assignee sync whenever any source is present, and the entire test suite would still pass: the existing outbound test passes assignment_source=None, and the new test only checks the same-integration case. Also untested: GroupAssignee.objects.deassign with assignment_source (the path sync_group_assignee_inbound actually takes on webhook-driven unassign).

[BUG] sync_group_assignee_outbound always includes the new `assignment_source_dict` key in the celery task kwargs (even as None), so during a rolling deploy new producers enqueue a kwarg the old workers' `sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue_id, user_id, assign)` signature does not accept. Any inbound assignment/unassignment enqueued by a new web node and executed by an old worker raises TypeError (unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source_dict'), the task fails without retrying against the new signature, and the outbound assignee sync to the external system is silently lost until the worker fleet is fully rolled — assignments made during the deploy window never propagate.

[BUG] The dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at module import time, so every AssignmentSource constructed via `from_integration` carries the same timestamp from when the worker/web process was booted, not when the assignment was queued. Any consumer that relies on `queued` to order, deduplicate, or age out assignment-sync events gets a stale process-start timestamp for every event; the field silently records wrong data rather than the actual enqueue time.

[ADVISORY] AssignmentSource round-trips through the celery queue as a JSON dict in which `queued` is serialized to a string, and `from_dict` does no type coercion, so the deserialized instance has `queued` as a str rather than the declared datetime. Once a source crosses the task boundary (the inbound-sync path in sync_group_assignee_inbound always populates it), any code that treats `queued` as a datetime (comparisons, .isoformat(), arithmetic) crashes with AttributeError/TypeError on the str; today nothing reads `queued`, but the first consumer to trust the type annotation hits this.

[BUG] The dataclass default `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated exactly once at module import time, so every AssignmentSource constructed via `from_integration` (and every `to_dict()` payload) carries the process-start timestamp rather than the time the assignment was actually queued. Any consumer of `queued` (and any audit/debugging of synced assignments) reads a timestamp that is hours or days stale from worker uptime, with no error surfaced; the field silently misrepresents when the assignment happened. This is verifiable mechanically: dataclass default expressions are evaluated once at class-definition time, not per instantiation.

[BUG] `assignment_source.to_dict()` embeds a non-JSON-serializable `datetime` (`queued`) into the Celery `apply_async` kwargs, so with Sentry's JSON task serializer the message publish raises synchronously instead of enqueueing the outbound sync. Every inbound assign/deassign webhook that reaches `sync_group_assignee_inbound` (the only path in this diff that constructs a source) crashes at `apply_async` with an encode error inside `GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign`, failing the inbound sync task instead of propagating the assignment; the tests miss this because `self.tasks()` executes tasks eagerly in-process and never exercises broker serialization. Even if the transport were changed to survive the datetime (e.g., stringified), `from_dict`'s `cls(**input_dict)` accepts it only because dataclasses perform no type validation, so the failure mode shifts rather than disappears.

[ADVISORY] The task gains a new kwarg `assignment_source_dict` with no producer/worker version tolerance, so during a rolling deploy messages published by new web nodes carry a key the old worker's task signature does not accept. Old workers raise TypeError (unexpected keyword argument) on every outbound assignee sync enqueued by new producers for the duration of the deploy window; each failure consumes a Celery retry and the assignment silently lags behind until workers are updated. A versioned payload (e.g., nested under a single opaque key consumed defensively) or tolerant-kwargs handling would avoid the skew.

[ADVISORY] `AssignmentSource.from_dict` returning None on any parse failure converts a corrupt or schema-drifted `assignment_source_dict` into 'no source', silently re-enabling the outbound sync the cycle guard was supposed to suppress. Any producer/consumer schema mismatch (extra field, renamed field, changed shape — e.g., a rolling deploy where a new field is added to the dict) makes `from_dict` raise TypeError inside the try, return None, and the task proceeds as if no source existed — the cycle-prevention check in `should_sync` is silently bypassed and ping-pong syncs resume with no log line and no error, while the caller sees a normal-looking successful sync.

[ADVISORY] The guard only suppresses the loop when the source integration equals the target integration, so two distinct integrations linked to the same group still form a cross-provider sync cycle (Jira inbound → outbound to GitHub → GitHub inbound → outbound to Jira → ...), despite the comment claiming this 'prevent[s] sync-cycles from occurring'. Organizations with two issue-sync integrations on the same project can enter an assignment ping-pong where each integration's webhook re-triggers the other's outbound task (each hop passes the guard because the source alternates between the two integration IDs), generating repeated outbound API calls and webhook traffic that only terminates if the external systems happen to suppress webhooks for no-op assignment changes; the misleading comment will steer future debuggers away from this exact loop.
